location_qualifier: northwest slopes of Mount Austen, inside the perimeter defense
source_locator: R2225: ch. X, The December Offensive
current_activity: pack howitzers on the northwest slopes of Mount Austen, supporting the attack
notes: Miller, ch. X: artillery support for the Mount Austen operation, which opened on 17 December 1942, was to be provided initially by the 246th Field Artillery Battalion and the 75-mm pack howitzers of the 2nd Battalion, 10th Marines. The Marine battalion moved its pack howitzers to the northwest slopes of Mount Austen, inside the perimeter defense. The exact occupation day is not named; 17 December is the opening of the operation it was assigned to support, not an invented occupation log. A landing day is not copied. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

notes: Miller, ch. XI: on 10 January 1943 the 75-mm pack howitzers of the 2nd Battalion, 10th Marines, were to support the fires of the 8th Field Artillery Battalion as a secondary mission, because the open terrain of the 27th Infantry's zone would permit profitable use of light artillery. location_qualifier: attached to the 147th Infantry on the coastal drive
notes: Zimmerman, ch. IX: in compliance with XIV Corps Operation Memorandum No. 11, 28 January 1943, the 2nd Battalion, 10th Marines, was attached to the 147th Infantry and continued in action. The place is the 147th's coastal sector west of the Matanikau in late January, not a new pin from a named beach that day. Confidence 0.5: Zimmerman only in this increment.
